reading.body:
James Lankford's recorded AI activity is legislative, not financial: three AI-related bills and twelve recorded votes, with no campaign money from AI companies or AI-focused committees in this data.

The three bills are narrow in scope. Two are transparency measures, the AI Systems Transparency Act and a resolution on religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in AI systems, both dated 2026-09-23. The third, the GUARD Act on user age-verification and responsible dialogue, dates to 2025-10-28. All three are sponsorship or cosponsorship, which signals position-taking rather than enacted law.

The twelve votes all concern a single bill, S. 2296, across 2025-09-02 to 2025-10-09. Lankford voted Yea on cloture, on the motion to proceed, on tabling an amendment, and on final passage, and split across the individual amendments. That is a procedural record on one measure, not a pattern across many.

What this does not show is money, committee assignments, or any link between these votes and data center siting, power procurement, or grid policy. The bills here address transparency and age verification, not compute or electricity. A reader looking for Lankford's position on the physical constraints on AI will not find it in this record.
